exposure: Cervical dilatation at inclusion (4 cm, 5 cm, ≥6 cm)
cohort: 99 nulliparous women with a single fetus in cephalic presentation and spontaneous labor onset at ≥37 weeks' gestation
finding: The occiput posterior position was the most common fetal position throughout the active phase of the first stage of labor, but occiput anterior became the most frequent position at full dilatation and after the head had descended below the midpelvic plane.
mod_finding: Six out of eight women who had a cesarean delivery had a fetus in the occiput posterior position throughout labor.
